question.text: Will the European Council's 26–27 November 2026 conclusions explicitly reference the EU's 22nd sanctions package against Russia?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves on the texts issued for the special European Council of 26–27 November 2026 and published by the Council on its meeting page (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2026/11/26-27/ ; conclusions are also collected at https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/european-council/conclusions/).

For resolution, "the conclusions" means every document published for that meeting as its conclusions or as a statement of heads of state or government — including the MFF conclusions, any separate Ukraine text or section, any annex, and any text published as being "firmly supported by [number] heads of state or government". Draft documents, statements by individual leaders and the Commission's own sanctions proposal are not part of it.

It resolves YES if any such text contains an explicit reference to a 22nd package of sanctions against Russia — that is, the ordinal "22nd" or "twenty-second" applied to a package of sanctions/restrictive measures targeting Russia, in any word order (for example "22nd package of sanctions", "22nd sanctions package", "twenty-second package of restrictive measures against Russia").

It resolves NO if none of those texts contains such a reference, or if no conclusions or statement of heads of state or government is published for the meeting.
question.fine_print:
A reference to sanctions against Russia that does not name the 22nd/twenty-second package (for example "welcomes the recent adoption of new sanctions"), or that names a different ordinal or a different country, resolves NO.

If the conclusions are published first in an initial form and later in a final form for the same meeting, the final published text governs.

If the Council's web pages cannot be loaded, the published conclusions PDF or the text as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.

research:
I haven't found anything that settles this yet. The Commission has not yet put forward the 22nd package, and the 16 November listings were a separate measure, not the 22nd package. Several news-API items say they were, but that is wrong.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17: The meeting page (consilium.europa.eu/.../2026/11/26-27/) returned HTTP 403, a browser check, so I couldn't read it. The Council press release of 16 November was also blocked (403). No conclusions can exist before 26 November in any case. [meeting page](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2026/11/26-27/)
- I could not find any leaked draft conclusions for the November summit. Drafts were leaked for October and June: [Table.Media, October draft](https://table.media/assets/documents/20261006_europe_euco_draft-conclusions.pdf).

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. The deciding question is whether the leaders name the "22nd" package by its number, whether it has been proposed by then or not.
- 2026-11-16: The Council listed 12 individuals and 101 entities, including 49 banks, oil refineries and online marketplaces (Decision (CFSP) 2026/2575). UNN describes this as separate from the comprehensive package, which is "still being prepared". Iz.ru and Pravda.com.ua call the listings the "22nd package", but that conflicts with UNN, with Kallas the same day, and with the Commission's statement in the background. [UNN](https://unn.ua/en/news/sanctions-against-russia-and-billions-of-euros-for-ukraine-key-outcomes-of-the-eu-council-meeting-on-november-16); [Ukrinform](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4185192-eu-imposes-sanctions-on-113-more-russian-individuals-and-entities.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: After the Foreign Affairs Council, Kallas said: "in the coming days we will present the 22nd package of sanctions." [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1237341.html)
- 2026-11-16: According to UNN, citing RFE/RL's Rikard Jozwiak, Commission and member-state talks on the package start this week, with the aim of approval "by Christmas". Possible contents include entry bans on Russian ex-combatants, tighter visa rules, a ban on Russian athletes and about 140 listings. [UNN](https://unn.ua/en/news/the-eu-will-present-its-22nd-package-of-sanctions-against-russia-in-the-coming-days-kallas)
- 2026-11-15/16: Czech MEP Ivan David said adoption in December 2026 is "quite likely", possibly including curbs on Russian diesel. [Lenta](https://lenta.ru/news/2026/11/16/raskryto-napolnenie-buduschego-paketa-antirossiyskih-sanktsiy-es/)
- 2026-11-12: In a joint statement, Costa and von der Leyen said: "The Commission will in parallel present its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia." Von der Leyen said this would come before the next European Council. [Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/12/joint-statement-by-president-costa-and-president-von-der-leyen-following-their-meeting-with-president-zelenskyy-in-dublin/); [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261112/d6745cb6a2a241deb4f8d86d093d08ff/c.html)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-10-15/16 conclusions: "welcome the recent adoption of the 21st sanctions package" (from the question background; the draft is reported by RFE/RL). [RFE/RL](https://www.rferl.org/amp/wider-europe-eu-summit-ukraine-funding-russia-sanctions-enlargement/33875302.html)
- 2026-06-01: A draft of the June conclusions, reported by Jozwiak, already "looks forward to the swift adoption of 21st sanctions package". That was eight days before the Commission formally presented it on 9 June. So the leaders have named a package by number before it was tabled. [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/european-council-welcomes-adoption-of-20th-sanctions-package--looks-forward-to-the-swift-adoption-of-21st-sanctions-package-reports-jozwiak); [Eurointegration](https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/eng/news/2026/06/9/7239336/)
- 2025-12-18: Points the other way. With the 20th package not yet presented, the conclusions said only "a new sanctions package... as soon as possible after its presentation in early 2026", with no number (based on a secondary report). [UNN](https://unn.ua/en/news/eu-prepares-20th-package-of-sanctions-against-russia-expected-in-early-2026-conclusions)
- Early 2026: The conclusions reportedly urged "rapid adoption of the 20th package" while Hungary and Slovakia were blocking it. That Ukraine text was not backed by all 27.
- Overall: the regular summits I checked in 2026 named the package by number. The exception was a summit held before the package was announced. This one is a special summit focused on the MFF, so the Ukraine text may be short or held up by Hungary or Merz. Texts "firmly supported by 25/26" still count for resolution.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The markets that were supplied (Graham Act, EU diesel ban, trilateral meeting and others) don't match it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- In the "coming days" (before 26 November): the Commission formally presents the 22nd package. If it is tabled, leaders are more likely to "call for swift adoption of the 22nd package".
- About 18-25 November: leaks of draft conclusions (Jozwiak/RFE/RL, Table.Media) would show the likely wording.
- 26-27 November: the special European Council itself. Risks include no conclusions on Ukraine at all, a text focused only on the MFF, or Merz linking Ukraine funding to the MFF talks. Hungary or Slovakia refusing could lead to a text "firmly supported by" fewer than 27 leaders, which would still count.
- The package will not be adopted before the summit (the target is December), so a "welcomes adoption" wording is very unlikely. The realistic route to YES is "calls for swift adoption of the 22nd package".

- Nothing has settled the question yet.
- Warning on the news feed: several items (Izvestia, Pravda.com.ua, 24tv) say the Council "adopted the 22nd package" on 16 Nov. That looks wrong. The 16 Nov action was 145 listings under existing sanctions regimes: 113 under the Ukraine territorial-integrity regime, plus hybrid and cyber listings. [Warbrief](https://warbrief.live/sanctions/eu-russia-sanctions-145-targets-50-banks-november-2026/), [Euronext/Reuters factbox](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/factbox-eu-expands-russia-sanctions-list-145-names-and-entities), [Steptoe](https://www.steptoe.com/en/news-publications/stepwise-risk-outlook/sanctions-update-november-16-2026.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-15/16: Czech MEP Ivan David told Izvestia the 22nd package will "quite likely" be adopted in December and may include restrictions on Russian diesel. [Izvestia](https://iz.ru/2202324/2026-11-16/v-evroparlamente-dopustili-novye-sanktcii-protiv-rossiiskogo-dizelia)
- Mid-Nov: Bloomberg reported adoption could come at the December Foreign Affairs Council. EU sources told European Pravda it would be ready by the end of November. [Warbrief](https://warbrief.live/sanctions/eu-russia-sanctions-145-targets-50-banks-november-2026/)
- 2026-11-12: Von der Leyen said in Dublin that the 22nd package and the Ukraine 2027 financing proposal will be presented before the next European Council. The Costa/von der Leyen joint statement says the Commission "will in parallel present its 22nd package." [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261112/d6745cb6a2a241deb4f8d86d093d08ff/c.html), [news.az](https://news.az/news/eu-to-unveil-22nd-russia-sanctions-package-and-ukraine-funding-plan-by-november-summit)
- Note: one Censor.net summary mentions a European Council on 17-18 December. I couldn't verify it because the page returned 403. If there is a regular December summit, the special November meeting may focus narrowly on the MFF and Ukraine financing. [Censor.net](https://censor.net/en/news/4033379/new-sanctions-and-a-support-package-for-ukraine-what-is-the-eu-preparing)

## 4. Base rates
- In 2026, conclusions named packages by ordinal in June ("calls for the swift adoption of the 21st") and October ("welcome… 21st"). The same pattern appears in earlier years, for example "welcomes the 19th package" in October 2025. Regular summits with a Ukraine section mention the pending or just-adopted package most of the time.
- Caveats:
  - This is a special summit called on the MFF. Special meetings sometimes have short, narrowly focused conclusions.
  - Ukraine texts have been issued as "firmly supported by 26" because of Hungary. The resolution criteria count those texts.
  - If the package is only proposed and not adopted by 26-27 Nov, the likely wording would be "calls for swift adoption of the 22nd package." That has precedent (June 2026).
- I found no systematic count of how often special European Councils mention sanctions packages.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the listed Kalshi or Polymarket markets matches this question. The closest are unrelated (EU lifting the Russian diesel ban by 31 Dec: 4.3% Yes). I found no Metaculus, Manifold or expert forecast on whether the conclusions will reference the 22nd package.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Commission's formal presentation of the 22nd package, expected "in the coming days" and before 26 Nov.
- Coreper and ambassador discussions of the package and of the Ukraine 2027 financing proposal, about €70bn.
- Draft conclusions circulating, which are often leaked to Politico, Euractiv or Reuters in the week before. These would show whether a Ukraine or sanctions paragraph is planned.
- Merz linking Ukraine funding to the MFF talks, and possible Hungarian or Slovak opposition. Either could lead to no Ukraine text, or a text "firmly supported by 26."
- 26-27 Nov summit: conclusions published on the evening of day 1 or on day 2.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. Conclusions are expected on 26 or 27 November 2026. For Yes, any text published for the meeting as conclusions or as a leaders' statement (including one "firmly supported by 26") must name the "22nd" or "twenty-second" sanctions package against Russia. The most likely wording would be "calls for the swift adoption of the 22nd package."

(b) No text exists yet. If nothing changed, nothing would be published that names the package, so the status quo is No. In practice, though, the outcome depends on what wording ends up in the Ukraine text.

(c) Base rate:
- **Regular summits:** 2025-2026 summits with a Ukraine section named the pending or just-adopted package by ordinal most of the time, roughly 75-85%. June and October 2026 both did.
- **Special summits:** these are a weaker reference class. Feb 2020 (MFF) produced no conclusions. Feb 2024 (MFF revision and Ukraine) and March 2025 (defence and Ukraine) referred to sanctions generically or not at all, as far as I recall. My estimate for special summits naming a package is about 30-40%.
- **Blend:** about 50%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The Costa/von der Leyen joint statement on 12 November explicitly tied the presentation of the 22nd package to the run-up to this European Council.
  - Kallas said on 16 November that it would be presented "in the coming days."
  - The June 2026 draft named the 21st package even before it was tabled.
  - A text "firmly supported by 26" still counts, which removes the Hungary veto risk.
- **For No:**
  - This is a special summit convened on the MFF and Ukraine financing, with the Merz linkage making it contentious.
  - It could produce no conclusions at all, or MFF-only text.
  - December 2025 used generic "new sanctions package" wording before the package was presented.
  - A possible regular December summit (17-18 December) could absorb the sanctions language instead.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** MFF talks stall and Merz holds up Ukraine funding. Leaders issue either nothing or a short statement on the MFF and Ukraine financing, with a generic line about "pressure on Russia."
- **Yes:** The Commission tables the package around 20-25 November. The Ukraine text, endorsed by 26 or 27 leaders, pairs the 2027 financing with "calls for the swift adoption of the 22nd sanctions package."

(f) I start from the blended 50%. The explicit linkage in Costa's own statement pushes me up a little. The real risk of no conclusions or narrow conclusions at a contentious MFF special summit pulls me back down. Net, I end close to even.

Probability: 50%

(a) The outcome will be known in about 10 days, when texts are published on 26-27 November 2026. For Yes, any conclusions or heads-of-state statement for the special European Council must contain the words "22nd" or "twenty-second" applied to a Russia sanctions package. That includes a text "firmly supported by 25 or 26" leaders.

(b) Status quo: no conclusions exist yet. If nothing changed, meaning no text is published or the text covers only the MFF, the question resolves No. The default drafting habit, however, leans toward naming the pending package whenever a Ukraine section exists.

(c) Base rate:
- Regular summits with a Ukraine section named the pending or just-adopted package by ordinal about 80-85% of the time in 2025-26. Examples are June 2026 ("calls for swift adoption of the 21st") and October 2026 ("welcome... 21st").
- The exception was December 2025, when the next package had not yet been presented.
- Special summits are less reliable. They sometimes produce no conclusions: the February 2020 MFF special summit issued none. When they do produce a Ukraine text, it often speaks only of "further sanctions" without a number.
- A blended base rate for this setup is about 50%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- On 12 November the Costa and von der Leyen joint statement explicitly linked the 22nd package to the run-up to this summit ("in parallel"), and von der Leyen promised it would be presented before the European Council.
- On 16 November Kallas said the package would come "in the coming days".
- The June 2026 draft named the 21st package even before it was formally tabled.
- Ukraine's 2027 financing is a formal agenda item, so a Ukraine text is likely. Texts supported by 25 or 26 leaders count.

Evidence for No:
- This is a special, contentious meeting convened on the MFF.
- Merz is linking Ukraine funding to the MFF, which risks a breakdown with no conclusions.
- The Ukraine text may focus narrowly on financing.
- The package adoption target is December, possibly with a regular summit on 17-18 December, so leaders might defer sanctions language to that meeting.
- If presentation of the package slips, the wording could become generic ("new sanctions package").

(e) No scenario: the MFF talks stall and the summit ends with only a short statement on Ukraine's financing or none at all. Alternatively, the Ukraine text says "further pressure on Russia, including through sanctions" without an ordinal.

Yes scenario: the Commission tables the package around 20-25 November. Leaders, or 26 of them, publish a Ukraine text calling for "the swift adoption of the 22nd sanctions package" alongside the 2027 financing language.

(f) I start from about 50%. I move up modestly because the package is explicitly being presented to coincide with this summit, and because drafters routinely name pending packages. I move partly back down for the real risk that a special summit fails to produce conclusions, or produces a narrowly focused text. That leaves a slightly better than even chance.

Probability: 55%

(a) The outcome will be known in about 10 days, when texts are published on 26-27 November 2026. For Yes, any conclusions text or statement of heads of state or government for that meeting must use the ordinal "22nd" or "twenty-second" for a package of sanctions against Russia. This can be the MFF conclusions, a Ukraine text, an annex or a text "firmly supported by 26". The most plausible wording is "calls for the swift adoption of the 22nd package".

(b) Status quo: no text exists yet. If nothing were published, or the texts covered only the MFF and financing, the question resolves No.

(c) Base rate: regular summits with a Ukraine section named the pending or just-adopted package in most cases in 2025-2026, roughly 70-80%. That includes June 2026, which named the 21st package eight days before it was tabled. The relevant reference class is narrower: special summits called on the MFF or financing. These often produce narrow conclusions or none at all:
- February 2020 MFF summit: no conclusions.
- July 2020 MFF summit: MFF conclusions only.
- February 2024 summit: mainly about the MFF revision.
- March 2025 Ukraine text: said only "further sanctions", with no package number.

For special summits, naming a package is perhaps 25-35%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On 12 November the Costa and von der Leyen joint statement explicitly paired the Ukraine 2027 financing with the 22nd package, which the Commission will present "in parallel" before this summit.
  - On 16 November Kallas said the package would be presented "in the coming days".
  - Since Ukraine financing is a core agenda item, a Ukraine text with a sanctions paragraph is likely.
  - The October 2026 and June 2026 conclusions both named the 21st package, and June did so before the package was tabled.
- **For No:**
  - This is a special MFF summit. Merz has threatened to link Ukraine funding to the MFF, so the meeting may break down without conclusions.
  - A regular European Council appears to be scheduled for 17-18 December, closer to the target adoption date ("by Christmas"). The sanctions wording may be saved for then.
  - In December 2025, with the package not yet presented, the conclusions used no number.

(e) No scenario: the MFF talks stall and leaders issue only a short MFF progress text, or nothing. Alternatively, a Ukraine financing text focuses on the €70bn gap and says "continue pressure on Russia" without a number.

Yes scenario: the Commission tables the 22nd package around 20-25 November. The Ukraine text, possibly "firmly supported by 26", then includes "calls for swift adoption of the 22nd sanctions package".

(f) I start from about 30% for special summits. I move up by about 15 points because the 22nd package was explicitly announced as a deliverable for this summit and Ukraine is on the agenda. Discounting for the risk that the meeting breaks down without conclusions and for the December summit, I end at about 45%.

Probability: 45%

For Yes, any published conclusions or "firmly supported by X" statement for the special European Council must contain the ordinal "22nd" or "twenty-second" applied to a Russia sanctions package. The most likely wording would be "calls for swift adoption of the 22nd sanctions package."

(b) Status quo: no text exists yet. If nothing changed, this resolves No, either because no conclusions are published or because the conclusions cover the MFF only.

(c) Base rate: regular summits in 2025-2026 with a Ukraine section name the current package by ordinal about 80% or more of the time:
- June 2026 named the 21st before it was even presented.
- October 2026 and October 2025 named the relevant package.

Special summits are a weaker reference class. The February 2020 MFF summit produced no conclusions at all. Special meetings often have narrow or partial texts, sometimes on Ukraine "firmly supported by 26." Blending these, I put the base rate for a special MFF/Ukraine summit at roughly 45-55%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- On 12 November, the Costa and von der Leyen joint statement explicitly linked the 22nd package to the summit timeline ("in parallel"). Von der Leyen said it would be presented before the European Council.
- On 16 November, Kallas said "in the coming days."
- Leaders have named packages by number even before they were tabled (the June 2026 draft).
- The summit's agenda includes Ukraine, so a sanctions or "pressure on Russia" paragraph is natural.

Evidence for No:
- The meeting is a special summit centred on the MFF.
- Merz is threatening to link Ukraine funding to the MFF talks, so the summit could end with no agreed text, or with a text limited to financing.
- Adoption is targeted "by Christmas," possibly with a regular December European Council (17-18 December, unverified), where sanctions language would more naturally sit.
